external_source: QRData women.csv (Quantitative Social Science 4.3.1), gold estimate (CC BY-NC 4.0, xxxiaol/QRData) — external anchor, no GADS recipe pinned (drafted lane by design)

local_attempt.note: 5 of 9 tasks failed: an invalid pandas kwarg on df.sample(), and two hallucinated Plotly calls (plotly.express.boxplot / plotly.express.table — neither exists in that API). Only the initial data-load step succeeded; no causal estimate of any kind was reached. Sharp contrast with the cloud run on this identical spec (9.2524, matching gold almost exactly) — this is the more expected direction per prior local-model drafted-lane evidence. See notes.md.

estimate.note: GADS canonical from cloud reference run (drafted lane, OLS ITT with GP-clustered SEs): +9.2524 drinking-water facilities, matching QRData's external gold (9.25) to the reported precision. The run went further than the gold answer unprompted: it also fit a 2SLS IV model using `reserved` as an instrument for `female`, estimating a LATE of +23.99 (p<0.0001) — a structural estimate the QRData question never asked for. Both are recorded; `estimate` here tracks the ITT figure that matches the external gold.

late_2sls.note: 2SLS LATE of female leadership (instrumented by reservation) on drinking-water facilities, from the same reference run. No external gold exists for this figure — QRData only asked for the reduced-form ITT effect. Recorded because the drafted plan produced it unprompted and it is methodologically the more complete answer to 'does becoming a female leader change water investment' (vs. the ITT's 'does the policy change it').
